coverage_model: implemented=complete for the stated claim_scope; partial=bounded executable slice with unresolved requirements; context_required=no safe automatic verdict without stated missing context; not_implemented=no executable check

unresolved_requirements: Complete technical-term classification and contextual dictionary-use decisions.
rules.claim_scope: Known dictionary approval status, ambiguity blockers, and unknown-term classification only.

unresolved_requirements: Occurrence-level grammatical role is not yet represented as a complete ambiguity set for every Issue 9 dictionary part of speech; deterministic Brill tagging is generic syntax evidence and cannot itself grant an STE part-of-speech verdict.
rules.claim_scope: Approved dictionary part-of-speech misuse when the deterministic generic occurrence projection maps uniquely to a compatible or incompatible STE dictionary role; unresolved or competing authoritative identities fail closed.

unresolved_requirements: Automatic approved-sense disambiguation.
rules.claim_scope: Occurrences with explicit project dictionary-meaning evidence only.

unresolved_requirements: Out-of-inventory verb/adjective forms that generic morphology cannot link unambiguously to one approved runtime lemma, and occurrence roles for which the generic morphology evidence does not establish a unique source-backed form identity.
rules.claim_scope: Generic verb inflections and comparative/superlative adjective forms are checked only after deterministic morphology links the occurrence to one approved runtime dictionary lemma; the source-backed runtime form inventory remains the approval authority.

unresolved_requirements: Classification of a candidate word into an Issue 9 technical-noun category.
rules.claim_scope: No automatic evaluation of technical-noun category eligibility.

unresolved_requirements: Automatic classification of unknown words as technical nouns or parts of technical nouns.
rules.claim_scope: Unknown prose terms are blocked pending project classification; the linter does not infer technical-noun status from prose.

unresolved_requirements: A complete ambiguity-preserving classification of every governed technical-noun occurrence as noun, adjective inside another technical noun, or prohibited verbal use is not yet available; the generic occurrence projection is evidence, not terminology authority.
rules.claim_scope: Governed technical-noun occurrences are rejected when deterministic occurrence evidence resolves them as verbal; unresolved grammatical identity fails closed.

unresolved_requirements: Automatic company, industry, or subject-field approval for technical nouns not supplied by governed project terminology.
rules.claim_scope: Deprecated governed project technical nouns are rejected; other approval authorities remain contextual.

unresolved_requirements: Judgment that a selected technical noun is short and easy for the intended reader to understand.
rules.claim_scope: No automatic evaluation of technical-noun brevity and ease of understanding.

unresolved_requirements: Automatic international-versus-regional/slang/jargon classification.
rules.claim_scope: Occurrences with explicit project technical-noun-scope evidence only.

unresolved_requirements: Document-wide item identity and technical-noun consistency.
rules.claim_scope: No automatic evaluation that the same item keeps the same technical noun across the document.

unresolved_requirements: Classification of a candidate verb into an Issue 9 technical-verb category.
rules.claim_scope: No automatic evaluation of technical-verb category eligibility.

unresolved_requirements: A complete ambiguity-preserving noun-versus-verb classification is not yet available for every governed technical-verb occurrence; generic occurrence tagging cannot by itself establish the full STE grammatical identity.
rules.claim_scope: Governed technical-verb occurrences are rejected when deterministic occurrence evidence resolves them as nominal; unresolved grammatical identity fails closed.

unresolved_requirements: A versioned offline American-English spelling authority and a governed project directive/specification/contract exception profile are not yet represented, so raw prose cannot be completely classified without occurrence-by-occurrence context evidence.
rules.claim_scope: Explicit project spelling evidence is checked, including the existing official-technical-name exception; STE-Lint does not infer American spelling or applicable external directives from raw prose.

unresolved_requirements: The full ambiguity set for noun-phrase boundaries and mixed grammatical identities is not represented; deterministic Brill POS/chunk evidence supplies one generic projection and therefore cannot prove every possible multi-word noun occurrence.
rules.claim_scope: Deterministically projected adjective/noun/proper-noun compounds with a nominal head are counted, with source hyphen groups counting as one word; unresolved phrase identity is not promoted to an STE verdict.

Approved governed technical nouns longer than three words use stable governed identity and representation authority: the full form must precede an authorized short-form, abbreviation, or acronym; unsupported synonym, legacy, overlong short-form, and shortened explicit-form representations are rejected. Hyphenated authorized short forms use the same governed identity, while Rule 8.2 separately governs direct-relation authority.

unresolved_requirements: Verb forms that deterministic generic morphology cannot link unambiguously to one approved source-backed runtime verb lemma remain unresolved.
rules.claim_scope: Observed generic verb inflections linked to one approved runtime dictionary verb are rejected when the source-backed verb paradigm does not contain the observed form; generic morphology cannot grant form approval.

unresolved_requirements: The complete Issue 9 allowed/prohibited verb-form and tense inventory is not yet represented as an exhaustive structural classifier; constructions outside the source-backed perfect/progressive/passive slices and their ambiguity sets remain unresolved.
rules.claim_scope: Source-backed direct perfect and progressive constructions are rejected, competing authoritative identities are blocked, and allowed simple-future WILL plus base-form use is not classified as complex.

unresolved_requirements: Complete pre-nominal participle-adjective recognition and the full allowed adjectival positions after BE/BECOME/STAY are not yet represented with all competing participle identities; cases outside the resolved passive/adjectival projections remain unresolved.
rules.claim_scope: Source-backed participles resolved as passive verbs are rejected and passive-versus-adjectival competing identities are blocked; direct perfect participles are also rejected.

unresolved_requirements: The complete source-defined auxiliary-construction inventory is not yet represented exhaustively; auxiliary constructions beyond classified perfect, passive, and progressive slices and their ambiguity sets remain unresolved.
rules.claim_scope: Source-backed perfect, passive, and progressive auxiliary constructions are rejected or blocked on competing authoritative identities; permitted simple-future WILL plus base form remains allowed.

unresolved_requirements: Every -ing occurrence is not yet represented with a complete ambiguity set covering governed technical-noun identity, modifier membership inside a technical noun, and verbal identity; generic POS evidence alone is insufficient for a complete rule verdict.
rules.claim_scope: Source-linked -ing forms resolved as progressive or other verbal use are rejected; governed technical-noun and governed technical-noun-modifier uses are allowed; competing allowed/prohibited identities are blocked.

unresolved_requirements: Descriptive passive actor-known/unknown semantics and passive-versus-adjectival ambiguity outside the resolved procedural passive frame.
rules.claim_scope: Resolved passive-verb participle in procedural mode only; descriptive passive and ambiguous participles are not automatically rejected.

unresolved_requirements: The rule requires identifying when a noun or other part of speech denotes an action and determining that an applicable approved verb describes that action; this semantic identity is not mechanically available from document syntax and terminology authority alone.
rules.claim_scope: Part-of-speech misuse already proven by dictionary-role evidence is reported, but STE-Lint does not infer action semantics or select an applicable approved verb from meaning.

unresolved_requirements: Sentence clarity and structural simplicity beyond the bounded Issue 9 length limits.
rules.claim_scope: Procedural and descriptive overlength sentence units provide a bounded short-sentence check; general sentence clarity remains unresolved.

unresolved_requirements: Omitted-word detection and non-deterministic or context-sensitive contraction-like forms.
rules.claim_scope: Deterministic contraction forms only; omitted words are not inferred.

unresolved_requirements: Determining that prose is sufficiently long or complex to require conversion to a vertical list remains an editorial/semantic decision; deterministic list structure and punctuation mechanics do not establish that trigger.
rules.claim_scope: Recognized CommonMark and STE-style vertical lists have deterministic colon, item-start capitalization, item punctuation, wrapped/nested structure, and sentence-versus-fragment mechanics; the linter does not decide when prose must become a list.

unresolved_requirements: Related-topic identity and selection of an appropriate connecting word or phrase.
rules.claim_scope: No automatic evaluation of sentence connection and discourse relationship.

unresolved_requirements: Noun/multi-word-noun identification plus contextual judgment of when an article or demonstrative adjective is applicable.
rules.claim_scope: No automatic evaluation of required articles or demonstrative adjectives before nouns.
Procedural sentences are deterministically checked against the 20-word limit using the shared Issue 9 canonical count-group projection.

unresolved_requirements: Instruction intent and action structures outside the resolved sentence-initial base-form plus coordinated base-verb frame, including implicit, nested, non-coordinated, simultaneous, and otherwise unresolved actions.
rules.claim_scope: Resolved multiple-action cardinality in procedural sentences recognized by shared Grammar v1 action structure only; simultaneous-action exceptions are not inferred.

unresolved_requirements: Imperative identity is not yet complete for command heads admitted only through governed technical-verb authority or other cases with no exact source-backed dictionary verb paradigm; those occurrences can be lexically valid while Rule 5.3 itself remains unresolved.
rules.claim_scope: Ordinary and condition-prefixed procedural commands with an exact source-backed dictionary identity must use the approved lexical base form; competing authoritative command-head identities are blocked.

unresolved_requirements: Condition semantics beyond the leading IF/WHEN structural slice.
rules.claim_scope: Leading IF/WHEN condition position and comma structure only.

unresolved_requirements: Instruction semantics in notes outside sentence-initial source-backed imperative candidates.
rules.claim_scope: Sentence-initial imperative candidates in NOTE blocks only; note sentence length is governed separately by descriptive Rule 6.3.

unresolved_requirements: Automatic information-order inference, gradual progression beyond explicit project ordering facts, and one-subject-per-sentence semantics.
rules.claim_scope: In descriptive text, uniquely resolved non-overlapping project-supplied semantic ordering facts are checked when the actual document clearly places the required after-target wholly before the required before-target.

unresolved_requirements: Identification and use of key words/key phrases that establish a logical text structure.
rules.claim_scope: No automatic evaluation of key-word/key-phrase logical structure.
Descriptive sentences are deterministically checked against the 25-word limit using the shared Issue 9 canonical count-group projection.

unresolved_requirements: Logical grouping of related information into paragraphs.
rules.claim_scope: No automatic evaluation of logical information grouping into paragraphs.

unresolved_requirements: Automatic topic inference and topic-sentence progression.
rules.claim_scope: Multiple distinct topics only when project topic evidence is supplied.
In the supported source model, descriptive CommonMark prose paragraph nodes are counted structurally and rejected above six sentences; list-item paragraphs are excluded as separate list structure.

unresolved_requirements: Automatic risk-level classification from prose, missing safety labels or symbols, and conflicting or insufficient project risk authority.
rules.claim_scope: Observed WARNING/CAUTION label versus one unambiguous supplied project safety level for the same validated safety block only.

unresolved_requirements: Complete safety command/condition semantics and multi-action analysis.
rules.claim_scope: WARNING/CAUTION opening and bounded imperative action structure only.

unresolved_requirements: Risk, consequence, explanation, and possible-result semantics.
rules.claim_scope: No automatic evaluation of safety-result explanation or consequence semantics.

Semicolons are prohibited in STE-authored text. Governed protected, immutable quoted external, code/verbatim, formula, and document-numbering spans are excluded; authored quotations and authored structural titles, placards, and labels remain in scope. No meaning-changing semicolon autofix is offered.

unresolved_requirements: Automatic semantic judgment of whether hyphenated words are directly related.
rules.claim_scope: Hyphen direct-relation judgment only when explicit project evidence is supplied.

unresolved_requirements: Automatic semantic classification of parenthetical use.
rules.claim_scope: Parenthesis-use category only when explicit project evidence is supplied.

In supported CommonMark and STE-style vertical-list structures, a terminal colon before a list ends the preceding count unit and wrapped or nested list items are counted as independent structural units with the applicable procedural/descriptive limit.
Parenthetical text groups count as one word through the shared Issue 9 canonical count-group projection.

The shared Issue 9 canonical count projection deterministically counts the specified one-word groups: numeric expressions; numbers with governed measurement units; governed abbreviations and acronyms; alphanumeric identifiers; quoted text; structural headings; explicitly governed titles, placards, and labels; and governed person, group, organization, and geopolitical proper nouns. It does not infer named entities with NER or guess unknown words are units.
Hyphenated token groups count as one word through the shared Issue 9 canonical count-group projection.

unresolved_requirements: Judgment that word-for-word replacement is insufficient and selection of a meaning-preserving alternative sentence construction.
rules.claim_scope: No automatic evaluation of when a different sentence construction is required.

unresolved_requirements: Automatic approved-meaning/context disambiguation for approved words.
rules.claim_scope: Explicit project evidence that an approved dictionary occurrence uses a non-approved meaning only.

unresolved_requirements: Automatic semantic recognition that an approved verb plus preposition combination has a combined meaning different from the approved meanings of its parts.
rules.claim_scope: Multiword occurrences explicitly classified by project authority as phrasal verbs are rejected; STE-Lint does not infer phrasal-verb meaning composition from raw text.

unresolved_requirements: Document-wide terminology and wording consistency for repeated work-step types and concepts.
rules.claim_scope: No automatic evaluation of terminology or wording consistency across a document.
